message: Column users.emailVerified uses `timestamp` (without time zone). Use `timestamptz` instead to avoid silent DST and cross-region bugs.
help: Postgres `timestamp` (without time zone) stores the literal wall-clock value with no timezone info. On read it's interpreted in the session's timezone, which differs across regions, OS configurations, and DST transitions — values silently shift on the boundary. `timestamptz` stores as UTC internally and converts on read; same 8-byte storage. Convert with: ALTER TABLE <t> ALTER COLUMN <c> TYPE timestamptz USING <c> AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' (note: this rewrites the table — use the expand-contract pattern on large tables).
suggested_fix:
-- Define new columns as timestamptz from the start:
emailVerified timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
